rows.question: My Limited Edition Alpha copy of False Orders reads "You decide whether and how one defending creature blocks, though you can't make a choice the defender couldn't legally make. Play after defender has chosen defense but before damage is dealt.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle

Verdict: Your Alpha copy's wording is obsolete — False Orders now does exactly what its current Oracle text says: it can only be cast in the declare blockers step, it removes a target creature the defending player controls from combat (unblocking a creature that had become blocked by only that creature), and it may then have that creature block an attacking creature of your choice.

Missing: None

Why: Under CR 108.1 the Oracle card reference, not the printed card, determines a card's wording, so the Alpha sentence about "you decide whether and how one defending creature blocks" no longer describes what the card does. The Oracle text instead makes this a declare-blockers-step-only instant that removes a blocking creature from combat and optionally re-assigns it as a blocker. This question is covered by a reviewed adjudication case that is marked verified, which specifies current Oracle text governs and that the overruled printing be named.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), as applied by the verified reviewed decision document `case.pvo-LEA-False-Orders`.

Quote [Oracle text — False Orders, card.38c5c952-8153-4d98-89b5-a75260383345]: "Cast this spell only during the declare blockers step.
Remove target creature defending player controls from combat. Creatures it was blocking that had become blocked by only that creature this combat become unblocked. You may have it block an attacking creature of your choice."

Quote [Printed text — Limited Edition Alpha, printing.7eb71ac4-796d-4011-9002-1129bc09c284, "originalText"]: "You decide whether and how one defending creature blocks, though you can't make a choice the defender couldn't legally make. Play after defender has chosen defense but before damage is dealt."

Quote [CR 108.1 — rule.108.1.2026-09-25]: "Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com."

Quote [Ruling, 2004-10-04, card.38c5c952-8153-4d98-89b5-a75260383345]: "If a creature is removed from being a blocker of a given attacker, any triggered abilities that would have happened because it was declared as a blocker still happen."

Quote [Reviewed decision — case.pvo-LEA-False-Orders, "expectedVerdict"]: "Current Oracle text governs under CR 108.1: \"Cast this spell only during the declare blockers step. Remove target creature defending player controls from combat. Creatures it was blocking that had become blocked by only that creature this combat become unblocked. You may have it block an attacking creature of your choice.\" The answer must reproduce this text completely and name the printing it overrules."

Rules: 108.1

Conflict: The Limited Edition Alpha printed wording (a decision-making effect on the defender's blocks, playable after defense is chosen) conflicts with the current Oracle wording (a declare-blockers-step instant that removes a creature from combat and may re-block). CR 108.1 resolves this in favour of the Oracle wording, so the printing printing.7eb71ac4-796d-4011-9002-1129bc09c284 (Limited Edition Alpha) is the overruled printing. Also note CR 108.1 appears twice in the corpus with identical text under two dates (rule.108.1.2026-08-07 and rule.108.1.2026-09-25); no textual disagreement between them.

Sources: card.38c5c952-8153-4d98-89b5-a75260383345, printing.7eb71ac4-796d-4011-9002-1129bc09c284, case.pvo-LEA-False-Orders, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, rule.108.1.2026-08-07

rows.question: My Unlimited Edition copy of Word of Command reads "You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Under current Oracle text, Word of Command makes you look at target opponent's hand, choose a card from it, control that player until the spell finishes resolving, and have that player play the chosen card if able — with mana-ability restrictions — and the printed "may not be countered after you have looked" clause is no longer in the card's text.
Missing: None
Why: Your Unlimited Edition wording is the printed text of the card, and a textDifference record flags that printing as a functional difference from current Oracle text. The reviewed decision document for this card states that Oracle governs, that the printed uncounterable clause was removed entirely, and that controlling the player replaced "you make all the decisions it calls for," adding mana-ability restrictions absent from the printed card. Two cautions on the evidence: the decision document's reviewMethod and confirmedByHuman fields are empty (only reviewedBy "joshua" and a review timestamp are recorded), and its claims array is empty, so the decision rests on the Oracle text and CR 108.1 rather than on linked claims.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording").
Quote [Oracle text, complete]: Look at target opponent's hand and choose a card from it. You control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving. The player plays that card if able. While doing so, the player can activate mana abilities only if they're from lands that player controls and only if mana they produce is spent to activate other mana abilities of lands the player controls and/or to play that card. If the chosen card is cast as a spell, you control the player while that spell is resolving.
Quote [Unlimited Edition printed text, complete]: You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand.
Quote [CR 108.1]: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card’s wording. A card’s Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.
Quote [CR 101.1]: Whenever a card’s text directly contradicts these rules, the card takes precedence. The card overrides only the rule that applies to that specific situation. The only exception is that a player can concede the game at any time (see rule 104.3a).
Quote [decision.Word-of-Command.0.257 resolution]: Oracle governs under CR 108.1: the printed uncounterable clause was removed entirely, and control of the player replaced "you make all the decisions it calls for", adding mana-ability restrictions that appear nowhere on the printed card.
Quote [card ruling, 2011-01-01]: Your opponent can't counter the Word of Command after letting you look at their hand, but they can attempt to counter the spell you force them to cast.
Rules: 108.1, 101.1 (also retrieved but not relied on: 100.2, 100.4, 510.1, 510.2, 608.2, 700.2)
Conflict: The card's stored 2011-01-01 ruling still says the opponent can't counter Word of Command after letting you look at their hand, while the current Oracle text contains no uncounterable clause and the decision document states the printed uncounterable clause "was removed entirely." CR 108.1 makes Oracle text the governing wording of the card, so the Oracle text and the decision govern; the retrieved evidence does not explain why the ruling remains on the card. The printed text also says "you make all the decisions it calls for," which the decision states was functionally replaced by controlling the player, so the printed wording loses on that point too.

rows.question: My Tempest copy of Mogg Fanatic reads "Sacrifice Mogg Fanatic: Mogg Fanatic deals 1 damage to target creature or player.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Your Tempest card's printed wording is superseded — the card's current Oracle text is "Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target."
Missing: None
Why: Under CR 108.1 you always use the Oracle card reference to determine a card's wording, so the 1997 Tempest wording on the physical card no longer describes what the card does. The ability's cost and effect are otherwise the same shape (sacrifice it, deal 1 damage), but the target has been broadened from "target creature or player" to "any target", which the glossary entry defines as target creature, player, planeswalker, or battle. A current ruling also notes that after Mogg Fanatic has dealt and been dealt combat damage it is too late to activate the ability before it's destroyed.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text for Mogg Fanatic, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), which overrides the Tempest printed wording; the reviewed decision document case.pvo-TMP-Mogg-Fanatic states the same verdict.

rows.question: Can Mogg Fanatic assign combat damage, sacrifice itself in response, and still deal that combat damage?
rows.answer:
Question type: interaction
Verdict: No — under the current rules Mogg Fanatic cannot deal its combat damage after being sacrificed in response, because combat damage is a turn-based action that doesn't use the stack and no player gets priority between assignment and dealing (this did work before the July 2009 Magic 2010 rules change, when combat damage used the stack).
Missing: None
Why: Assigning combat damage is a turn-based action, and all assigned combat damage is then dealt simultaneously, also as a turn-based action; nothing in that window is a spell or ability on the stack, so nobody can respond. The card's own sacrifice ability is an activated ability, which can only be activated when a player has priority, and no priority is given between damage being assigned and damage being dealt. A verified adjudication case for this exact question reaches the same result and attributes the difference to the change in the combat damage rules rather than to any change in Mogg Fanatic's activated ability, which did not materially change.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text of Mogg Fanatic plus CR 510.1 and 510.2 (combat damage step), corroborated by the verified adjudication case case.rv-Mogg-Fanatic; CR 108.1 governs printed-vs-Oracle wording generally.
Quote — Oracle text (card.7efd5d62-6da2-428a-98e3-5b842f668656): "Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target."
Quote — CR 510.1 (rule.510.1.2026-09-25): "First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then the defending player announces how each blocking creature assigns its combat damage. This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack. A player assigns a creature’s combat damage according to the following rules:"
Quote — CR 510.2 (rule.510.2.2026-09-25): "Second, all combat damage that’s been assigned is dealt simultaneously. This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack. No player has the chance to cast spells or activate abilities between the time combat damage is assigned and the time it’s dealt."
Quote — Card ruling, Wizards, published 2016-06-08: "Once Mogg Fanatic has dealt and been dealt combat damage, it’s too late to activate its ability before it’s destroyed."
Quote — CR 108.1 (rule.108.1.2026-09-25): "Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card’s wording. A card’s Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com."
Quote — Tempest printing, original printed text (printing.ca2ecfd4-c874-4468-8601-87aa110d5a00, set Tempest, released 1997-10-14): "Sacrifice Mogg Fanatic: Mogg Fanatic deals 1 damage to target creature or player."
Quote — Verified adjudication case expected verdict (case.rv-Mogg-Fanatic): "No, not under the current rules. Before the Magic 2010 rules change in July 2009 combat damage used the stack, so this worked. The activated ability relevant to this interaction did not materially change; the rules governing combat damage did."

Rules: 510.1, 510.2, 108.1
Conflict: The Tempest printed text ("target creature or player") and the current Oracle text ("any target") disagree on legal targets; Oracle governs, per CR 108.1. That wording difference is not what decides this question. The decisive point is that pre-July-2009 rules put combat damage on the stack (allowing the sacrifice to resolve first), while CR 510.1–510.2 as retrieved make both damage assignment and damage dealing turn-based actions that don't use the stack — the current rules win.

rows.question: When Word of Command resolves, who controls the opponent, and for how long?
rows.answer:
Question type: currentWording
Verdict: You (the caster of Word of Command) control the target opponent until Word of Command finishes resolving, and you also control that player while the chosen card's spell resolves if it is cast as a spell.
Missing: None
Why: The current Oracle text assigns control to the spell's controller and fixes its duration by reference to the spell finishing resolution, extending it through the resolution of the forced spell if one is cast. The reviewed adjudication case on file for this exact question confirms the same reading, and CR 108.1 makes the Oracle text the governing wording rather than any earlier printed text. The rulings retrieved add only supporting detail about what controlling that player lets you see and do.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text of Word of Command, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), as applied by the verified reviewed decision case.rv-Word-of-Command.

Quote Oracle text (complete): Look at target opponent's hand and choose a card from it. You control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving. The player plays that card if able. While doing so, the player can activate mana abilities only if they're from lands that player controls and only if mana they produce is spent to activate other mana abilities of lands the player controls and/or to play that card. If the chosen card is cast as a spell, you control the player while that spell is resolving.

Quote CR 108.1 (2026-09-25, identical text at 2026-08-07): Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording. A card's Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.

The complete current Oracle text must be quoted, including the mana-ability restrictions, which appear nowhere on the Alpha printing.

Quote ruling (2016-07-13): While controlling another player, you can see all cards in the game that player can see. This includes cards in that player's hand, face-down cards that player controls, and any cards in that player's library the player may look at.

Rules: 108.1

The reviewed decisions note that earlier printed wording differs (control of the player replaced "you make all the decisions it calls for", and mana-ability restrictions are absent from the Alpha printing), but CR 108.1 makes the current Oracle text control, so the printed text does not affect the answer.

rows.question: Is Chaos Orb's physical flip requirement still part of its Oracle text?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Yes. Current Oracle text still requires the physical flip — flipping the card onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot, and it must turn over completely at least once during the flip.
Missing: None
Why: The card document for Chaos Orb (current as of 2026-09-18) carries Oracle wording that retains both the height requirement and the "turns over completely at least once" condition, so the physical flip was retemplated rather than removed. The differences between the printed card and Oracle are elsewhere: Oracle adds {T} to the activation cost, restricts the destroyed permanents to nontoken ones, and phrases the destruction as what the artifact touches rather than "any cards in play." A verified adjudication case for this exact question records the same expected verdict, and CR 108.1 directs that Oracle wording governs a card's wording. Note that the 2019 ruling quoted below gives a different text for Old School play specifically; that is an Old School format text, not the current Oracle wording.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text of Chaos Orb (source.scryfall.2026-09-18), under CR 108.1, with the verified adjudication case case.rv-Chaos-Orb.
Quote oracle text: "{1}, {T}: If this artifact is on the battlefield, flip it onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot. If this artifact turns over completely at least once during the flip, destroy all nontoken permanents it touches. Then destroy this artifact."
Quote printed text (Limited Edition Alpha): "{1}: Flip Chaos Orb onto the playing area from a height of at least one foot. Chaos Orb must turn completely over at least once or it is discarded with no effect. When Chaos Orb lands, any cards in play that it touches are destroyed, as is Chaos Orb."
Quote ruling (2019-01-27): "If you are playing Chaos Orb in the Old School format, the card's text is “{1}, {T}: Choose a nontoken permanent on the battlefield. If Chaos Orb is on the battlefield, flip Chaos Orb onto the battlefield from a height of at least one foot. If Chaos Orb turns over completely at least once during the flip, and lands resting on the chosen permanent, destroy that permanent. Then destroy Chaos Orb.”"
Quote ruling (2004-10-04): "It must flip 360 degrees (that's what \"flip\" means). And this flip must be in the air and not in your hand."
Rules: 108.1
Conflict: The printed texts (LEA/LEB/2ED) say "{1}:" and destroy "any cards in play", while Oracle says "{1}, {T}:" and destroys "all nontoken permanents it touches" — under CR 108.1 Oracle wins on those points, but the flip requirement is present in both, so nothing conflicts on the flip itself. A separate model-assisted, unconfirmed decision (decision.Chaos-Orb.0.346) lists only the {T} and token differences and does not address the flip requirement; the verified case governs here.
Sources: card.edb455f4-8dc9-4b7c-b25c-cb51b7dfbb41, case.rv-Chaos-Orb, printing.92274971-7c4a-4326-b0fe-75e2d124f718, printing.6bec436c-2869-432a-b3cf-633a58af6d4c, printing.7a601041-926f-40fd-8106-39099b87806f, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, rule.108.1.2026-08-07, source.scryfall.2026-09-18, source.cr.2026-09-25, decision.Chaos-Orb.0.346

rows.question: My Alpha Lightning Bolt says 'one target'. Can I still point it at a planeswalker?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Yes — your Alpha Lightning Bolt can target a planeswalker, because the current Oracle text says "any target," and Oracle wording governs over the printed wording.
Missing: None.
Why: Your Alpha copy's printed instruction is not the text the card is played with today. Current Oracle text routes Lightning Bolt at "any target," and the glossary definition of "any target" expressly includes a planeswalker among the legal choices. A verified case document and two draft decisions on this exact card reach the same result: the printed "one target" wording yields to Oracle under CR 108.1. I retrieved the CR 108.1 paragraph text itself, but I did not retrieve a paragraph body for CR 115.4, which the glossary entry cites; the mapping of "any target" to creature, player, planeswalker, or battle therefore comes from the retrieved glossary entry, not from the rule paragraph.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text, under CR 108.1 ("Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card's wording"), as applied by the verified adjudication case for this card; the glossary term "Any Target" supplies the meaning of the Oracle phrasing.
Quote Oracle text: Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target.
Quote printed text (Limited Edition Alpha, printing.d573ef03-4730-45aa-93dd-e45ac1dbaf4a): Lightning Bolt does 3 damage to one target.
Quote glossary entry "Any Target": A spell or ability may require “any target.” “Any target” is the same as “target creature, player, planeswalker, or battle.” See rule 115.4.
Quote CR 108.1: Use the Oracle card reference when determining a card’s wording. A card’s Oracle text can be found using the Gatherer card database at Gatherer.Wizards.com.
Rules: 108.1, 115.4
Conflict: The Alpha printed wording ("one target") conflicts with current Oracle wording ("any target"). Oracle wins under CR 108.1. Secondarily, among the case documents, case.rv-Lightning-Bolt carries reviewState "verified" while decision.Lightning-Bolt.0.6 and decision.Lightning-Bolt.0.636 are model-assisted drafts marked "unconfirmed"; the verified case and the drafts agree, so the drafts add nothing that changes the outcome.
Sources: card.4457ed35-7c10-48c8-9776-456485fdf070, printing.d573ef03-4730-45aa-93dd-e45ac1dbaf4a, diff.printing.d573ef03-4730-45aa-93dd-e45ac1dbaf4a, glossary.Any-Target, rule.108.1.2026-08-07, rule.108.1.2026-09-25, case.rv-Lightning-Bolt, case.pvo-LEB-Lightning-Bolt, decision.Lightning-Bolt.0.6, decision.Lightning-Bolt.0.636
